title: Estar a punto de: on the edge of the missile crisis

sections.content: You know *estar a punto de* + infinitive from B1 Unit 1: it says that something was about to happen. In the *imperfecto* it often sets the scene before an event (*estaba a punto de llegar cuando…*); in the *indefinido* (*estuvo a punto de*) it says that something nearly happened. Both fit the Cuban missile crisis, when the world nearly saw a war.

items.spanish: En octubre de 1962 el mundo estuvo a punto de entrar en una guerra nuclear.
items.english: In October 1962 the world came close to entering a nuclear war.

items.spanish: Algunos barcos soviéticos estaban a punto de llegar a la línea del bloqueo cuando se detuvieron.
items.english: Some Soviet ships were about to reach the line of the blockade when they stopped.

items.spanish: Los exiliados estaban a punto de desembarcar cuando empezó el ataque.
items.english: The exiles were about to land when the attack began.

items.spanish: El bloqueo estuvo a punto de causar un choque entre los barcos.
items.english: The blockade almost caused a clash between the ships.

sections.content: *Estar a punto de* is always followed by an infinitive (*estaba a punto de llegar*). The action did not happen, or had not happened yet: use *estaba a punto de* to set the scene and a preterite for the event that came next.
